_doc: EXTERNAL-SURFACE-PARITY-W1 CH3 — the SoT for every published surface OUTSIDE this repo that carries a claim derived from live /api/performance-public. Every gate this project owns lives inside crypto-quant-signal-mcp and is therefore structurally blind to a listing in someone else's catalog: that is why C3c of OPS-DOCKER-CATALOG-* corrected servers/algovault-remote/tools.json BY HAND while server.yaml and readme.md sat stale beside it, and why nothing noticed for months. Read by scripts/check-external-surface-parity.mjs. Missing, unparseable, or carrying an empty surfaces[] => EXTERNAL_SURFACE_PARITY_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3 — never a pass.
_enumeration_policy: ENUMERATE, DO NOT DETECT. A surface absent from surfaces[] is invisible to every gate we own, so the completeness of this list IS the deliverable — the canary can only ever verify what is named here. CLAUDE.md's consumer-registry LAW ('a shared primitive used by >=2 repos gets a CONSUMER REGISTRY naming every installation; detection is strictly weaker than enumeration') is applied here to PUBLISHED CLAIMS rather than to executables. Publishing a new external listing without adding its row is the defect; adding the row is the whole cost.
_no_producer_finding: MEASURED 2026-08-24, and it is the substantive finding of this registry: NONE of these surfaces has a refresh producer. In-repo landing/*.html and README.md are re-baked nightly by ops/cron/snapshot-landing-daily.sh from scripts/snapshot-landing-manifest.json; nothing whatsoever re-bakes a file in a third-party catalog repo. So every row below is refresh_mechanism=MANUAL by structure, not by neglect, and the spec's alternative parity leg — 'or its refresh mechanism ran more recently than the last SoT change' — can NEVER pass for these rows. That is not a gap in the canary; it is the honest report, and it is why the figures are written in a FORWARD-STABLE rounded-down form that stays true as the values grow rather than an exact figure that re-staleens the next day.
_freshness_control: raw.githubusercontent.com is CDN-cached at max-age=300 in BOTH ref forms — the ref form does NOT control freshness (CLAUDE.md, measured twice). For a verification read the control is a cache-buster or a pinned SHA. The canary appends a cache-buster query param; it deliberately does NOT pin a SHA, because pinning would make the canary verify the commit we wrote instead of the branch head anyone can push to, which is the tautology this registry exists to avoid.

_tolerance_vocabulary.EXACT_ROUNDED: The published literal must equal the live SoT value rounded to `dp` decimal places. Deliberately NOT a band: the surface publishes at 1dp, so the tightest honest statement is that it round-trips at its own stated precision, and any band wide enough to be quiet is wide enough to have accepted the real defect — 91.6% published against a live 91.71% is 0.11pp, which a 0.5pp or even 0.2pp band would have passed. A firing here is a genuine one-line correction, never noise.
_tolerance_vocabulary.FLOOR_BOUNDED: For a monotonic count published as `<floor>+`. PASS iff floor <= live < floor + max_steps*step. The lower leg catches a SoT regression; the upper leg is the BOUNDED GAP that a bare floor lacks — CLAUDE.md: 'when two quantities should track each other, assert a BOUNDED GAP; a one-sided inequality catches only sign violations and is blind to magnitude drift.' A bare floor is exactly why `1,300+ assets` read as true against a live 1,748 and `375,000+ calls` against 508,080. `step` is the rounding granularity the literal was written at, so the bound scales with the claim instead of being a magic number. max_steps DEFAULTS TO 1 — the published floor must BE the floor of the live value at that granularity, so `1,700+` becomes due for rewrite exactly when assets reach 1,800. max_steps=2 was the first draft and is measurably too weak: `375,000+` against a live 508,080 PASSES a 2-step bound at 100k granularity, i.e. the bound would have accepted the very defect this wave exists to fix.

surfaces.refresh_mechanism: MANUAL — no producer. Corrected only by a dispatched wave; no cron, no deploy hook, no injector reaches this repo.

forbidden.venue_count: Listing copy publishes no venue/exchange count (standing policy, Mr.1 2026-07-17). Asserted, not merely intended.

surfaces.refresh_mechanism: MANUAL — no producer. Same repo and same absence of any producer as the row above.

assert_no_sot_figures.reason: This file carries tool descriptions, not performance claims, and its only numerals today are parameter limits and defaults (10, 25, 50, 200, 2000). An EMPTY fields[] would make the canary verify nothing for this row — a vacuity hole in the very registry built to close one. So the assertion is inverted and stays falsifiable: the file must contain NO SoT-derived figure. If a future edit puts a win-rate percentage or a five-plus-digit call/asset count in here, the canary FAILS until the figure is registered as a field with a tolerance.
assert_no_sot_figures.note: Drift of the tool DESCRIPTIONS themselves against live tools/list is a different subject with its own owner (tests/unit/tool-description-forward-stability.test.ts governs the in-repo side). This row asserts only the numeric-claim property.
